legend: You are given a directed graph with n$$$n$$$ nodes and m$$$m$$$ edges. The color of the i$$$i$$$-th edge is ci$$$c_i$$$.
We call a path (does not have to be a simple path) colorful iff it does not have two consecutive edges of the same color.
Find all nodes x$$$x$$$ such that there exist a colorful path starting from 1$$$1$$$ and ending at x$$$x$$$.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤105$$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n≤106$$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$, 0≤m≤106$$$0 \le m \le 10^6$$$) — the number of nodes and the number of edges.

Next m$$$m$$$ lines describe edges: i$$$i$$$-th line contains three integers ui,vi,ci$$$u_i, v_i, c_i$$$ (1≤ui,vi,≤n$$$1 \le u_i, v_i, \le n$$$; ui≠vi$$$u_i \ne v_i$$$; 1≤ci≤m$$$1 \le c_i \le m$$$) — defining the edge from ui$$$u_i$$$ to vi$$$v_i$$$ of color ci$$$c_i$$$.
The sum of n$$$n$$$ and the sum of m$$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 106$$$10^6$$$.
output: For each test case, output all the nodes x$$$x$$$ such that there exist a colorful path starting from 1$$$1$$$ and ending at x$$$x$$$ in ascending order.
